title: Chicago nights: Paul Mares, Baby Dodds and giving away the Pollack drums
summary: He recalls the Blackhawk and the Three Deuces in Chicago and gives Baby Dodds a set of drums he had kept from Pollack.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You ever go to the PNM barbecue, I guess the name ever was?
PNM barbecue, Paul Merares' place in Chicago?
I, I went there a couple of times. Mm-hmm. They were up on the north side around, around the Chicago River. Mm-hmm. Um, we used to go to the Three Deuces of a lot.

That's when Baby Dots was playing on, and then, uh, well, when we'd get through at the, in fact, tell me about, about that thing. When we was playing at the Blackhawk, the second time, the second time that we played the Blackhawk, I'd been, I'd been working, the first time I went on that, I was working with the drum factory, designing drums and stuff, so you'd get the new drums and all. Mm-hmm. So, in the meantime, when we left New York, after we got, I left Pollock's band, I had a set of drums that Pollock, I, I kept, see, because Pollock had owed me some money. Mm-hmm. So, I kept these drums and then, and the one cymbal that he wanted, he wanted that cymbal more than anything in the world, and I wouldn't, I wouldn't give it to him. Mm-hmm. I said, when you pay me my money, he owed me around $250, $300. Mm-hmm. And then, one night, as I would play, and all, he didn't pay a seat. Well, anyway, it's a long story, and I had them in, in, in storage in New York. So, when I went to, when I went, uh, with the Crosby band, went to the New York hotel and all, I got it out of storage when we were coming back to Chicago. And, uh, and Baby Dots was playing in, in, in the, in the Three Deuces. And what I did, uh, I put him in my car, and brought him down, down, down there, and I said, I got something for you. And I, I, I, he, he said he needed a set of drums, the drums were bad. So, I gave him this whole set of drums, I brought them all down there. I mean, I, the, the guy was kissing me and everything, he was so happy. And, uh, it was wonderful, you know. And I was glad I could give, give that set of drums to somebody that, that appreciated that type of drums. Mm-hmm. So, that, that was it on, on that.
But, did you see Paul much in Chicago?
I didn't see Paul much. I knew his wife there, and, uh, what, what, uh, what, uh, what was the name, I can't remember. His wife? Yeah.
Something like Tootsie or Tina or? Tina. Tina, yeah, that was it. I can't remember. Yeah, Tina. Yeah.

But, I mean, I, I was, uh, you see, working at the, at the, at the Blackhawk, we, we, we played about the same time that they, they had their, they going over there, see. And, uh, of course, after we got through at night, we'd get through about two o'clock in the morning. So, it was, by the time we lived, we left the, up around, on, on, on, on, on, on, on, on the north side there by the, by the, that was the name of a hotel. What, uh, what street? I can't think of the name of that.
You mean the Blackhawk? Not the Blackhawk?

No, no, I'm talking of the north side, way uptown, uptown around, uh, Well, don't worry. Well, anyway, we lived up that way, see, so by the time we, we, we, get, get in our cars and go home, it's about three o'clock in the morning and so forth. And, my wife didn't come down to Woodbury all the time and she was all alone in, in this hotel room. And I used to try and get, get home as fast as I could, you know. Mm-hmm. But sometimes I, I would go down, uh, with the guys and I'd call her up and say, Well, we're going down to here so-and-so at the Sunset, uh, uh, or, here's Zooty and the guys down there, you know, at the Eagles, uh, on, uh, on, uh, on the piano player, Boogie Whirer piano player, uh, Mead Lux Lewis, you know, something like that.

So, she, she understood, you know, you know, so forth. But I, I didn't get a chance to go much to, uh, to, around on the north side at that time. Mm-hmm. Because that, that was over on the other side of the river, see. So, I, I didn't get much chance to, to, to go around with Paul there. No.
